about: Admitted cells of the estate genome: each passed its birth check on a fresh clone when this was made. Route by lane.

cells.name: break-it
cells.purpose: A secure ingest gateway that proves who sent each record, in what order and in exactly what shape, on the raw bytes before any software parses it, and refuses everything else with the stage that stopped it.

lane.accepts: one raw packet as bytes (hex), the pinned public key table of its senders, and each sender's last admitted counter
lane.refuses: an already-parsed record: the gate checks bytes before parsing, so a record that skipped it cannot be vouched for

interface.in: {packet, pinned, last}: the packet in hex, sender id to 32-byte Ed25519 public key in hex, sender id to last counter; to judge, a claim: the stage
interface.out: admitted with the frozen parsed message, or refused with the stage (size, magic, schema, sender, signature, counter, error) and a reason

judge.what: a claimed gate decision for a packet is right when break-it's own decide(), with the pinned keys and counters, stops it at the same stage or admits it

cells.name: browser-swarm
cells.purpose: Runs a swarm of small AI cells in a browser tab and releases only the answers its checks verify: an answer from your documents must be the source's own words, or it is withheld with the reason.

lane.accepts: a question about the documents in its signed corpus
lane.refuses: questions no signed paragraph covers, and paragraphs whose signature no longer matches

interface.in: {"question":"<text>"} to ask; an answer record {question,answer,source} to audit
interface.out: a released answer with its source and character offsets, or a refusal naming the check that stopped it

judge.what: an answer record is right when the answer is the source's own words, in the sentence that best matches the question, carrying enough of the question's words, and not in a sentence that gives orders

cells.name: consumer-rights-cell
cells.purpose: Answers questions about the Consumer Rights Act 2015, Part 1 from its own text only: the best-supported sentence, word for word, with its passage and character offsets. Refuses questions outside its lane.

lane.accepts: a question about the Consumer Rights Act 2015, Part 1
lane.refuses: questions whose words the the Consumer Rights Act 2015, Part 1 text does not use

interface.in: {"question":"<text>"} to ask (node genome/act.mjs); an answer record {question,source,start,end,text} to audit
interface.out: a verified answer record (passage id, character offsets, the exact sentence), or a refusal that says why

judge.what: an answer record is right when its text is exactly the cited passage's characters at its offsets and that passage uses at least the lane share of the question's content words

cells.name: docdecdemo
cells.purpose: Answers questions only from your documents: finds the passage, copies the answer word for word with its offsets, and refuses what no passage supports.

lane.accepts: a question about the documents in its index
lane.refuses: questions its indexed documents do not cover

interface.in: {"question":"<text>"} to ask; an answer record {source,start,end,text} to audit
interface.out: an answer record with its source and character offsets, or a refusal naming the check that stopped it

judge.what: an answer record is right when its words are exactly the cited passage's characters at its offsets (claim C6)

cells.name: estate-genome
cells.purpose: The birth check: admits a part as a cell only when it describes itself, proves or refuses its output, can be shed reversibly, and refuses past its lane.

lane.accepts: a folder holding a part (seed.json and its genome hooks) to check
lane.refuses: anything that is not a part to check

interface.in: {"part":"<folder>"} to check, or {"part":"<folder>","verdict":"cell|part"} to confirm a verdict
interface.out: the verdict record {"part","verdict","line"}: a verdict per trait, and admitted or not

judge.what: a claimed verdict on a part is right when re-running the birth check on that part gives the same verdict

cells.name: falljustice
cells.purpose: Helps a person with no lawyer draft a Letter Before Action on the correct modern statute, and checks the law any letter cites against a hand-verified table. Not legal advice; local and encrypted.

lane.accepts: the text of a letter or passage that cites law, to check every citation against the hand-verified table
lane.refuses: a request for legal advice or a prediction of the outcome: that is not a text to check, and this tool is not a lawyer

interface.in: {text}: the letter or passage; to judge, a claim: vouched, unvouched, pseudo-law or none
interface.out: each citation read from the text with whether the verified table vouches for it, the pseudo-law flag, the scope notice

judge.what: a claimed verdict on a letter's citations is right when falljustice's own checkLetter() gives the same verdict: it vouches only for the hand-verified table and flags pseudo-law first

cells.name: genome-fold
cells.purpose: Folds a folder of plain-text or markdown documents into a verified question-answering cell: an index, an extractive answerer with no language model, a judge, a measured lane and a drafted seed, shipped only when the birth check admits it.

lane.accepts: a corpus of plain-text or markdown documents to fold into a cell
lane.refuses: anything that is not a text corpus: no documents, text with no content words, or a question with no corpus

interface.in: {"corpus":[{"name":"<file>","text":"<text>"}]} to fold; with a record {question,source,start,end,text} to audit
interface.out: a cell folder (seed.json, index, judge, lane, act hook) admitted by the birth check, or the list of what is missing

judge.what: an answer record from a folded corpus is right when its text is exactly the cited passage's characters at its offsets and that passage uses at least the folded lane share of the question's content words

cells.name: house-standard
cells.purpose: The one starting point for every repository in the estate: a dark design kit (a living crystal hero, receipt cards, a stack, a glass that runs on the visitor's device, an honest expander) and a ship gate that holds any built page to seven rules, so a page leads with numbers it can prove and keeps its limits one click away.

lane.accepts: a built web page, as its HTML
lane.refuses: anything that is not a page: there is nothing to hold to the standard

interface.in: {"html":"<!doctype html>…the whole page…"}
interface.out: verified when the page meets all seven rules of the house standard; unverified when it fails any; refused when what is given is not a page

judge.what: a page ships only when it has the kit, greets no one with a wall of text, sources every receipt, leaves nothing unfinished, shows its failures, wears the house identity and keeps the house rules

cells.name: kar-alerttriage
cells.purpose: Turns a flood of SIEM, EDR or IDS alerts into a short ranked list of incidents: repeats become bursts, routine noise is set aside, related bursts link, and every incident's score is shown as arithmetic, with no AI model judging.

lane.accepts: a list of alerts (Wazuh, Suricata eve.json, Elastic/ECS or flat rows) with at least one it can place in time, and optional options {burstGap, incidentGap, backgroundShare, backgroundMinHours}
lane.refuses: anything that is not alerts to triage, such as a request to block an address or act on an incident

interface.in: {"alerts":[<alert>],"options":{...}} plus, to audit, a claimed ranking {"ranking":[{"kind":"incident|background","rules":["<rule id>"]}]} in rank order
interface.out: {ok:true, groups:[{kind, score, first, last, alerts, bursts, hosts, addresses, rules, marks}], stats}, or {ok:false, why}

judge.what: a claimed ranking is right when AlertTriage's own run on the same alerts and options gives the same groups, of the same kind and the same rules, in the same order

cells.name: kar-benfordgap
cells.purpose: A first-digit fraud screen for a column of amounts: compares how often each first digit appears with Benford's Law and gives one verdict, with chi-square, Nigrini's MAD and the digits to look at first, with no AI judge.

lane.accepts: a column of amounts (numbers or ledger strings such as £1,200.00 or (350.50)) with at least one usable nonzero amount, and optionally the sample floor
lane.refuses: anything that is not a list of amounts, such as a CSV pasted as one string, a list with no usable amount, or a question about whether someone committed fraud

interface.in: {"values":[<amount>,...],"minN":<optional floor>,"verdict":"<claimed verdict>"}
interface.out: one verdict (too-few, close, acceptable, marginal or nonconformity) and which test gave it, with the counts, chi-square, MAD and z per digit

judge.what: a claimed screen verdict for a column is right when BenfordGap's own audit gives that same verdict for those amounts; a conforming verdict is a screen result, never proof the data is honest

cells.name: kar-citelock
cells.purpose: Checks a claim against the sources it cites, with fixed rules and no AI judge: VERIFIED only when every quotation is word for word in a cited source and every content word and number is in a cited source; otherwise REFUSED, with the reason for each failed part and the offsets of every check.

lane.accepts: a claim (text) with the 1 to 50 sources it cites, as {claim, sources}
lane.refuses: anything that is not a claim with its sources: questions, requests for an opinion, and judgements of meaning or of whether a source is true

interface.in: {"claim":"<text, with optional [id] markers>","sources":[{"id":"s1","text":"<source text>"}]}
interface.out: VERIFIED or REFUSED, the reason for each failed part, and the trace: every quotation, number and content word checked, with the source and the offsets where it was found

judge.what: a claim is verified when the kernel's verify() finds every quotation word for word in a cited source and every content word and number outside the quotations in a cited source

cells.name: kar-conform
cells.purpose: Checks an AI model's structured output against its JSON Schema contract with no AI judge: PASS or FAIL with the exact path of every violation, and a hash that tells reformatting apart from real drift.

lane.accepts: a JSON Schema (an object, or true or false) and one model output as its raw text
lane.refuses: anything that is not a schema and an output's text, such as a list in place of a schema, an output already parsed into an object, or a question about whether the output is true

interface.in: {"schema":<JSON Schema>,"json":"<the model output's raw text>"}
interface.out: PASS or FAIL with every violation's path and message, and the output's canonical SHA-256 hash

judge.what: a model output is right when it parses as JSON and Kar-Conform's own validator finds no violation of the schema; a rule the validator does not check fails the output rather than passing it; shape, never truth

cells.name: kar-consentdecay
cells.purpose: Answers whether an act is still covered by consent: consent was granted for one scope, weakens by half every half-life, and is gone once a matching revocation lands. Anything it cannot match is refused, never estimated.

lane.accepts: a grant {scope, grantedAt, halfLife, minStrength?, revocations?} and an act {scope, tick}
lane.refuses: anything that is not a grant and an act it can rule on, such as a request to grant or record consent on someone's behalf

interface.in: {"grant":{"scope":"<purpose>","grantedAt":<n>,"halfLife":<n>},"act":{"scope":"<purpose>","tick":<n>}} plus, to audit, a claimed ruling {"ruling":"COVERED|EXPIRED|REFUSE-UNKNOWN"}
interface.out: {ok:true, ruling: COVERED|EXPIRED|REFUSE-UNKNOWN, why?, strength?}, or {ok:false, why} for a grant or act it cannot read

judge.what: a claimed ruling is right when ConsentDecay's own ruling for that grant and act is the same: a revoked or decayed consent is never covered

cells.name: kar-driftscore
cells.purpose: Scores how far a model's inputs have drifted: one number from 0 (identical) to 1 (nothing shared) between two label-count distributions, the total variation distance, with no AI judge.

lane.accepts: two label-count distributions (what the model used to see, what it sees now), each with non-negative counts and a total above zero
lane.refuses: anything that is not two scorable distributions, such as raw text, a single list, negative or empty counts, or a request to retrain a model

interface.in: {"distA":{"<label>":<count>},"distB":{"<label>":<count>},"score":<claimed drift>}
interface.out: the drift score from 0 to 1, or a refusal saying which count is wrong

judge.what: a claimed drift score is right when DriftScore's own kernel recomputes the same total variation distance for those two distributions, to six decimal places

cells.name: kar-fairshare
cells.purpose: Splits a pot that cannot pay every claim in full, to the penny, by one of four standard rules (proportional, equal awards, equal losses, the Talmud rule), with leftover pence settled by name so list order never matters.

lane.accepts: a pot in whole pence, the claimants {id, claim} in whole pence, and a rule: proportional, cea, cel or talmud
lane.refuses: anything that is not a split to compute, such as a request to pay the claimants

interface.in: {"pot":<pence>,"claims":[{"id":"<name>","claim":<pence>}],"rule":"proportional|cea|cel|talmud"} plus, to audit, a claimed payout {"pence":[<pence per claimant, in list order>]}
interface.out: {ok:true, rule, pot, total, paid, leftover, shortfall, rows:[{id, claim, pence, exact, lost}]}, or {ok:false, error}

judge.what: a claimed payout is right when it is, claimant for claimant, the pence FairShare's own exact split gives under that rule

cells.name: kar-glyphguard
cells.purpose: Finds the tricks that hide in characters (invisible characters, lookalike letters, bidi overrides, hidden tag text, styled letters) with no AI judge, and re-checks any report it exported against the text, byte for byte.

lane.accepts: a text and the Glyphguard report exported for it (the report, with its input and report hashes)
lane.refuses: anything that is not a text with its exported report, such as a bare text with no report, or a question about whether a message is safe

interface.in: {"text":"<the text>","export":{"tool":"glyphguard","version","inputHash","reportHash","report":{...}}}
interface.out: whether the report matches a fresh scan of the text, and whether its input and report hashes match

judge.what: an exported report is right when Glyphguard's own re-check finds a fresh scan of the text gives the same report and neither hash disagrees; clean means these known tricks were not found, never that the text is safe

cells.name: kar-irhelper
cells.purpose: Incident-response helper for hosts you own: will not start without a written authorization naming the host, reads evidence with fixed read-only commands, proposes each step with its undo, never acts itself, and logs every step in a hash chain.

lane.accepts: an incident response on a host its written authorization names: {scope: who authorized, when, why, which hosts, until when; host; now}
lane.refuses: a host the authorization does not name, an expired or incomplete authorization, and any request to act without a person approving it

interface.in: {"scope":{"authorizedBy":"<person>","authorizedAt":"<ISO time>","expires":"<ISO time>","purpose":"<why>","hosts":["<host>"]},"host":"<host>","now":"<ISO time>"}; to audit a record, {"log":[<entry>],"anchor":"<recorded hash>"?}
interface.out: a scope check {ok, why[], summary}; facts and proposals with exact commands and undo; a hash-chained log whose check gives {ok, entries, brokenAt, anchoredAt}

judge.what: an incident record is right when IR Helper's own log check finds every entry's number, link and hash intact and, when an anchor is given, the anchor still in the chain

cells.name: kar-isolationgate
cells.purpose: Release gate for shared totals: remembers which contributors were in every total already released, and refuses any new release that could be subtracted against them to single out fewer than k parties (the differencing attack).

lane.accepts: a gate state {k, released: lists of contributor ids} and the contributor ids of the next total to release
lane.refuses: anything that is not a release to decide, such as a request for one contributor's own figure

interface.in: {"state":{"k":<whole n, 2 or more>,"released":[["<id>"]]},"contributors":["<id>"]} plus, to audit, a claimed decision {"release":<bool>}
interface.out: {ok:true, state, releases, size} when the release is safe; {ok:false, why, against?, size?, k?} when it is refused or the input is malformed

judge.what: a claimed decision is right when IsolationGate's own propose makes the same call: release only when no difference, reverse difference or overlap with any earlier release isolates fewer than k

cells.name: kar-quorumfloor
cells.purpose: Settles a vote's turnout floor exactly: decisive votes (yes plus no) as a percentage of everyone present, cross-multiplied in whole numbers so no rounding can pass a failed vote or fail a passed one.

lane.accepts: a list of votes {weight, choice: yes|no|abstain} with whole non-negative weights, and a whole-number threshold from 0 to 100 percent
lane.refuses: anything that is not a ballot it can settle exactly, such as a request to declare the result or act on it

interface.in: {"votes":[{"weight":<whole n>,"choice":"yes|no|abstain"}],"thresholdPercent":<0-100>} plus, to audit, a claimed result {"clears":<bool>,"margin":<whole n>}
interface.out: {ok:true, value:{clears, margin}}, or {ok:false, why} for a ballot it cannot settle exactly

judge.what: a claimed result is right when QuorumFloor's own whole-number check gives the same clears and the same exact margin

cells.name: kar-quorumgate
cells.purpose: Decides whether an action collected a real quorum: each distinct voter counted once at a valid weight, the weight behind each choice tallied, and the total checked against the threshold.

lane.accepts: a ballot: a list of votes {voter, weight, choice} and a non-negative threshold
lane.refuses: anything that is not a ballot it can count, such as a request to carry out the action a vote approved

interface.in: {"entries":[{"voter":"<id>","weight":<n>,"choice":"<option>"}],"threshold":<n>} plus, to audit, a claimed outcome {"met":<bool>,"winner":"<option>"|null}
interface.out: {ok, met, total, winner, tally}, or {ok:false, why} for a ballot it cannot count

judge.what: a claimed outcome is right when QuorumGate's own tally, counting each distinct voter once, reaches the same met and the same winner

cells.name: kar-quorumveil
cells.purpose: Guards a private sum: contributions are released only as masked shares, the total is unveiled only when at least three masked shares are present, and noise is added at unveiling from a caller seed.

lane.accepts: an unveil request: a list of shares {masked, data}, a whole-number seed and a whole-number noise scale of 0 or more
lane.refuses: anything that is not an unveil request, such as a request to read one contributor's raw number

interface.in: {"shares":[{"masked":true,"data":[<n>]}],"seed":<whole n>,"noiseScale":<whole n>} plus, to audit, a claimed released total {"sum":[<n>]}
interface.out: {ok:true, sum, noised, quorum, live}, or {ok:false, why} when the release is refused (below quorum, an unmasked share, mismatched lengths)

judge.what: a claimed released total is right only when QuorumVeil's own unveil releases it (quorum met, every share masked) and gives exactly that total

cells.name: kar-redactseal
cells.purpose: Redacts named spans of a document and seals the removals in a hash chain, so a later disclosure of what was removed can be proven faithful to the sealed redaction without trusting whoever discloses it.

lane.accepts: a document and the spans to remove {text, spans}, or a sealed redaction and a disclosure to check {redacted, positions, revealed, seal}
lane.refuses: anything that is neither, such as a request to show what was removed without the original

interface.in: {"text":"<doc>","spans":[{"start":<n>,"end":<n>}]} to seal; {"redacted":"<doc>","positions":[{"start":<n>,"end":<n>}],"revealed":["<text>"],"seal":<n>} to check a disclosure
interface.out: {ok, redacted, positions, seal, spanCount} for a seal; {ok, valid, why?, original?} for a disclosure check; {ok:false, why} for input it cannot read

judge.what: a disclosure is right when RedactSeal's own check finds every marker, every length, every position and the recomputed hash chain equal to the seal

cells.name: kar-scopeguard
cells.purpose: Checks how an AI coding agent got its green: reads the change and flags every test skipped, loosened or deleted, every CI step told to ignore failures, and every file outside what the task allowed.

lane.accepts: a change as unified diff text, with an optional scope file and the agent's own summary of what it changed
lane.refuses: anything that is not a readable diff and scope, such as an agent's claim that the tests pass with no change attached

interface.in: {"diff":"<unified diff>","scope":"<.scopeguard text, optional>","claim":"<the agent's summary, optional>"}
interface.out: a verdict (clean, review or flagged) with every finding's rule, file, line and exact text

judge.what: a change is right only when ScopeGuard's own audit finds nothing at all (verdict clean); any high or review finding means it is not verified

cells.name: kar-spendwall
cells.purpose: A spend wall for an AI agent's paid model calls: a daily cap checked before every call, a ceiling reserved on every call, a hard stop, and a ledger an independent auditor re-adds.

lane.accepts: the wall's own ledger: its reservation, settlement and refusal lines, as one JSON array
lane.refuses: anything that is not a ledger, such as a request to raise the cap, move the stop or make a call

interface.in: [{"seq","kind":"reserve|settle|refuse",...}] (the ledger lines, oldest first)
interface.out: the audit: rows K1, K2, K3, K4 and O, each passed, failed or undecided, with what was measured

judge.what: a ledger is right only when the wall's own audit passes every row: each call carried the evidence the cheaper tiers failed, no day over its cap, the total never past the stop, kar-tally re-adds every line, and no call cost more than its ceiling

cells.name: kar-tally
cells.purpose: Recomputes an AI agent's spend log from its budget cap and proves the claimed balances add up, no entry is missing and the cap was never exceeded, with no AI judge.

lane.accepts: a spend log: a budget cap, a starting sequence number and a non-empty list of entries, each with its cost and claimed running balance
lane.refuses: anything that is not a spend log, such as a question, a bill in prose or a request to pay or move money

interface.in: {"cap":<number>,"startSeq":<integer>,"entries":[{"seq","actor","action","cost","balance"}]}
interface.out: a verdict, PASS or FAIL, naming every violation, with each entry's recomputed balance

judge.what: a spend log is right when Kar-Tally's own recompute finds every claimed balance equal to the cap minus the costs so far, no gap in the sequence, and the cap never exceeded

cells.name: kar-veil
cells.purpose: Provable redaction with no AI judge: commit a document to a root, then publish a redacted version whose proof anyone can check against that root without ever seeing the hidden lines.

lane.accepts: a veil proof (v2, or the older v1), with the root published before the redaction and optionally the redacted document as received
lane.refuses: anything that is not a well-formed proof, or a trusted root that is not 64 hex characters, such as a request to reveal a hidden line

interface.in: {"proof":{"kind":"kar-veil-proof-v2","root","lineCount","visible","hidden"},"trustedRoot":"<64 hex>","received":"<optional redacted text>"}
interface.out: VERIFIED, CONSISTENT, BREACHED or MALFORMED, with every issue and every warning named

judge.what: a redaction proof is right only when Veil's own verify recomputes it to its stated root and to the trusted root with no warning: a v1 proof (whose faults the kernel names) or a proof with no trusted root is never verified

cells.name: konomi-ablate
cells.purpose: Leave-one-out ablation for system prompts: removes each clause, tests with an exact sign test whether the eval really moved, and certifies a batch of deletions only after the joint run holds.

lane.accepts: a system prompt and the per-item eval scores of its baseline and its clause-removed variants
lane.refuses: a prompt with no eval scores, or a single-clause prompt: there is nothing to compare

interface.in: {prompt, results}: results maps baseline, without-<i> and joint to per-item scores; to judge, a claim: the clause indices certified for deletion
interface.out: a verdict per clause (DEAD, LOAD_BEARING, HARMFUL, PROTECTED, INCONCLUSIVE), the joint check, and the certified set

judge.what: a claimed set of deletable clauses is right when konomi-ablate's own analyse() certifies exactly that set from the same scores

cells.name: konomi-clean
cells.purpose: Checks whether evaluation items appear in a reference corpus, by containment rather than Jaccard, item by item, with what the headline score becomes once the leaked items are left out.

lane.accepts: an evaluation item's text and a reference corpus of documents to check it against
lane.refuses: an item with no reference corpus, or a corpus that is not a list of documents

interface.in: {item, reference}: the item (text or {id, text}) and the corpus documents; to judge, a claim: EXACT, NEAR, PARTIAL or CLEAN
interface.out: a per-item verdict (EXACT, NEAR, PARTIAL or CLEAN) with its containment, and the score impact across a set

judge.what: a claimed contamination verdict for an item is right when konomi-clean's own checkItem(), at its default shingle size and thresholds, gives the same verdict against that corpus

cells.name: konomi-export
cells.purpose: Turns graded responses into SFT and DPO training rows, and refuses the pairs that would poison them: ties, grading gaps, unexplained gaps and any pair that trades away safety or grounding.

lane.accepts: a candidate pair of graded responses (each a seven-axis vector and its criterion verdicts)
lane.refuses: raw, ungraded responses: grade them with a rubric first

interface.in: {a, b} graded sides; to judge, a claim: the chosen side ('a' or 'b') or the refusal name
interface.out: a DPO pair with its margin and the criteria that separate the sides, or a named refusal with its reason

judge.what: a claimed outcome for a candidate pair is right when konomi-export's own buildPair() gives the same outcome: the same chosen side, or the same named refusal

cells.name: konomi-regress
cells.purpose: Compares two model-evaluation runs or refuses to: inadmissible comparisons throw, movement is paired item by item, and the gate names every hole a headline number hides.

lane.accepts: two recorded evaluation runs (rubric fingerprint, model version, item vectors) to compare
lane.refuses: questions about which model is better that come without two recorded runs

interface.in: {before, after} run records; to judge, a claim: the hole kinds the gate should find, or 'inadmissible'
interface.out: an admissibility verdict, paired movement, per-axis deltas, an exact sign test and the gate's named holes

judge.what: a claimed reading of a comparison is right when konomi-regress's own compare and gate find exactly the holes it names (or refuse the comparison as inadmissible)

cells.name: openkonomi
cells.purpose: The checkpoint for an AI agent: every action is checked against its grant (a capability level per resource, and a call and spend budget) before it happens, and anything outside the grant is refused with a reason.

lane.accepts: a grant (capabilities per resource, optional call and spend budget) and one action request naming its resource and level
lane.refuses: free text an agent was told to follow, such as a skill's setup instructions: that is not a request with a resource and level

interface.in: {grant: {caps, budget}, request: {resource, level, cost}}; to judge, a claim: allowed, or the refusal code
interface.out: allowed, or refused with its code (capability, budget_calls, budget_spend, unknown_resource) and a reason

judge.what: a claimed decision for an action is right when openkonomi's own permits() gives the same code for that request under that grant

cells.name: pixelwhisperer
cells.purpose: Draws the face of every Kardlings card from the card's own facts, with whole numbers only, and reads a sealed card file back face up only when it is exactly the file its record makes.

lane.accepts: a sealed card file: a PNG that carries its Kardlings card record, as base64 text
lane.refuses: anything that is not a card file, such as a plain picture with no card record, damaged or non-canonical base64, or a request to draw a card

interface.in: {"png":"<the card file, base64>"}
interface.out: face up with the card's record, or face down with the reason (how many pixels differ and where, or what else the file carries)

judge.what: a card file is right only when PixelWhisperer's own reader makes the whole file again from the record it carries and every byte matches (face up); a face that is not the one its record draws stays face down

cells.name: seam-check
cells.purpose: A GitHub Action that checks a pull request's stated intent against the organisation's own repositories and says, before the merge, whether the org already owns this, partly owns it, or it is new.

lane.accepts: a pull request title and body that state an intent of two or more words, and the org's repositories as {name, desc} entries
lane.refuses: a pull request whose title is a label rather than an intent, or no list of the org's repositories

interface.in: {title, body, shadow}: the PR text and the org's repositories; to judge, a claim: already-owned, partly-owned or novel
interface.out: the verdict with the repositories that cover the intent and their support, and the PR comment

judge.what: a claimed ownership verdict for a pull request is right when seam-check's own checkOf() gives the same verdict against the same repositories

cells.name: the-climb
cells.purpose: Runs a small AI model in a browser tab through a calculation it gets wrong at the first try, and rules on every step by code: a true step is kept, a false one is dropped and split into smaller steps, until the checker says the answer is right or the climb stops.

lane.accepts: one step of working: arithmetic with numbers, + - × ÷, powers and brackets, and the value claimed for it
lane.refuses: anything that is not arithmetic it can work out exactly: words, letters, implied multiplication, division by zero

interface.out: verified when the working comes to exactly that value, unverified when it does not, refused when the step cannot be read

judge.what: a step is right when its working, worked out in exact whole-number fractions, equals the value claimed for it

cells.name: the-crystal
cells.purpose: Grows a calculation as a crystal in a browser tab: a small AI model is asked one single step at a time, a step it states exactly right bonds, a step it gets wrong is split into smaller steps, and a step with nothing smaller dissolves. A crystal that completes is right.

lane.accepts: one cell: one operation on two numbers (26 × 12), and a reply to it
lane.refuses: anything that is not a single step of arithmetic: words, a bare number, working with more than one operation

interface.out: verified when the reply states that cell's value exactly, unverified when it does not, refused when the cell is not a single step

judge.what: a reply bonds a cell only by stating that cell's value exactly right: a true line about the cell, or the bare value

cells.name: the-distillation
cells.purpose: Trains a small AI model only on its own working that exact arithmetic verified, then measures it cold (one try, no checker) on problems it never saw. The trained weights are kept only if it is right more often and no more confidently wrong, and a later round starts from them only when a person grants it. Every round is sealed and can be judged again from its records.

lane.accepts: a calculation and a reply of worked steps ending in ANSWER: n, offered as a training example
lane.refuses: anything that is not an exact calculation: there is no check for it, so nothing can be verified or trained on

interface.out: verified when every line is one step and exactly true and the answer is the calculation's own; unverified when any line or the answer is not; refused when what is asked is not a calculation

judge.what: a reply may be trained on only when every line of its working is a single true step and its answer is the calculation's own

cells.name: the-seed
cells.purpose: A handful of small files that grow verified software one cell at a time: a model writes each cell, code checks it down to an axiom floor the seed works out itself, a cell that proves out is sealed, and one that cannot is dissolved.

lane.accepts: a whole-number sum of + - and ×, with brackets, and a reply to it
lane.refuses: anything the floor cannot work out exactly: words, letters, division, fractions, or a reply with no whole number in it

interface.out: verified when the sum comes to exactly the whole number the reply ends on, unverified when it does not, refused when the sum or the reply cannot be read

judge.what: a reply is right when the sum, worked out in exact whole numbers with no rounding, equals the whole number the reply ends on

cells.name: the-verifier-set
cells.purpose: Answers questions about documents in a browser tab with a small AI model, and labels how true each answer is. A cited figure must be in the document word for word, a rule written as a formula must pass its tests, a claim is decided by an exact solver, and each step is checked by exact arithmetic. Where a figure is missing or stated two ways, it gives no answer and says why.

lane.accepts: a document, something it states once with one figure (the unit price), and a quote offered as stating it
lane.refuses: a figure the document does not state, states two ways, or that is asked for in words the document does not use

interface.in: {"document":"The unit price is 126 pounds.\nThe order size is 12 crates.","cell":"the unit price","reply":"The unit price is 126 pounds."}
interface.out: verified when the quote is in the document letter for letter, in the line that states the cell, with its one figure; unverified when it is not; refused when the document cannot give the figure

judge.what: a quote cites a figure only when it is the document's own words, begun and ended at the edge of a word or number, in the line that is about what was asked

cells.name: witness-kit
cells.purpose: Wires a mutation gate into a repository honestly: finds the kernel and test pairs it can gate, names the lane (wire it, add discipline to an existing mutator, or refuse as theatre) and writes the pinned workflow.

lane.accepts: a repository's file listing (as git ls-files prints it) and whether the repository is an ES module package
lane.refuses: a request with no file listing, such as 'add a gate to my project' on its own

interface.in: {files, esm}: repo-relative paths and a boolean; to judge, a claim: the lane A, B or THEATRE
interface.out: the lane with its reason and notes, and for lane A a pinned workflow that reads every verdict

judge.what: a claimed lane for a repository is right when witness-kit's own detect() and plan() name the same lane for that file listing
